paras: As players make their way through the new Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, folks are also looking for any hint about what might come next. A 3DS remake of the sequel followed four years after the Ocarina of Time one, so it doesn’t seem an unreasonable next step. Some of the “hints” players are pointing at were in the original Ocarina of Time, but they can still be read as hints toward Majora’s Mask. The original Majora’s Mask launched just two years after Ocarina of Time in 2000, and the game reuses a fair bit of Ocarina’s assets and character models, so a few of the characters that would appear in a hypothetical Majora’s Mask remake are in Ocarina of Time. The primary antagonist in Majora’s Mask is a Skull Kid and they appear in Ocarina, as does the Happy Mask Salesman, who is also a central character in the sequel.

Comments made by the Skull Kid in the Ocarina of Time remake have spawned discussion around a potential Majora’s Mask remake, but as others have pointed out, the dialogue people are pointing to references a quest within Ocarina of Time, though if you haven’t played the game in a while, you might think it’s a direct nod to the events of Majora’s Mask.

paras: Image: Nintendo EPD/Nintendo via Polygon Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Sign in to your Polygon.com account follow Follow followed Followed Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Speedrunners have had their hands on the Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for a couple of days now, and some funky tricks have already been discovered. In particular, the remake's addition of a jumping mechanic has enabled new speedrunning tactics that just weren't possible in the Nintendo 64 original or its 3DS remake.

Videos from YouTubers like Kethaldo and Knightpohtayto, as well as Bluesky user Mircacle, show how actor jumping is essentially a glitched super jump that players can do with certain aimable tools in Ocarina of Time. To perform the trick, players have to find a movable object, or "actor," in the game's environments, like a chest or movable tombstone. When standing on it, players then have to shoot, press the lock-on button (ZL by default) before it's done being used, and then jump as soon as the animation ends.

By doing this, Link can jump much higher than he is supposed to. When used at certain parts of Ocarina of Time's levels, it's possible to jump even higher and skip massive swaths of the game. Right now, it's easiest to pull off when using the hookshot, so actor jumps are worth attempting once you get it.

paras: The anticipated remake of the seminal Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time dropped this week. Lifelong fans are returning to a familiar but altered Hyrule. Wind Waker’s camera can launch little Toon Link into hyperspeed across the ocean. Skyward Sword’s opening menu seems to exist in some kind of temporal pocket dimension. Some of the classics, like the building-bounding ‘Hookshot Jump,’ appear to be viable. One of the most popular pieces of tech revolves around open chests. Last year saw some of newly-installed creative director Demna’s first big red carpet moments, like stars Elle Fanning and Doja Cat appearing in their boldest looks by the Italian label. This year saw things amp up even more: Kim Kardashian played with her enduring love of the cut-out in a Bordeaux-toned sequin dress, while Parker Posey looked radiant in a sparkling white kaftan. Sienna Miller made the case for the LSD (the Little Silver Dress) while Rose Huntington-Whiteley went to glamorous extremes with some serious skin on show—all were care of Gucci.

And while Gucci was well represented across the evening, striking looks were also served courtesy of Valentino, Saint Laurent, and Chanel. pg:https://www.thehindu.com/news/interna.desc: Rubio defends Trump’s Iran war as necessary to curb nuclear threats, despite unpopularity and political backlash.
paras: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday (November 7, 2026) that President Donald Trump launched the war against Iran, even if it was not “necessarily popular”, to safeguard the world from the country's nuclear ambitions.

He would not comment directly about the Republican wipeout in Tuesday's (November 3) elections, which delivered a resounding rebuke to Mr. Trump. The unpopularity of the Iran war and its impact on gasoline prices and other parts of the economy helped Democrats seize control of Congress.

Asked about Vice-President J.D. Vance's social media post last week that largely blamed the war for the Republican losses, Mr. Rubio told reporters that Mr. Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and worked to stop the Islamic Republic from pursuing a nuclear weapon.

pg:https://www.azernews.az/region/267069.desc: The 31st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change officially opens today in Antalya, Türkiye.
paras: The 31st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change officially opens today in Antalya, Türkiye.
The 12-day conference, which Türkiye is hosting for the first time, will bring together representatives from 196 parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change and the European Union.
According to Türkiye's Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change, preparations have been completed at the designated COP31 venue in Antalya.

pg:https://www.theguardian.com/business/.desc: Asian and European markets follow US tech rout with many analysts predicting more waves of selling to come
paras: European and Asian stock markets fell sharply on Friday after the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterms triggered a rout in US tech stocks a day earlier.

A sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by sharp falls in Asian stock markets on Friday. The investor sentiment then reached London, where the market was, at one stage, poised for its worst day since March.

The FTSE 100 index, which tracks blue-chip shares listed in London, was down as much as 254 points, or 2.35%, at 10,528 points during a wave of selling in morning trading. But by the close of the day it had clawed back some of its losses to be down 1%, helped by a rise in US stocks when Wall Street reopened.

pg:https://qazinform.com/news/cop31-clim.desc: The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change will begin Monday in Türkiye's Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, bringing together heads of state, senior officials, academics, and civil society representatives from around the world, Anadolu reported.
paras: First held in Berlin in 1995, the annual summit provides a platform for countries party to the convention to assess progress in combating climate change, develop common solutions, and make decisions shaping global climate policies.
Türkiye will preside over this year's conference, which runs on Nov. 9-20 and addresses key decisions on sustainable development and climate policies.

A 1.1 million-square-meter (11.8 million-square-foot) venue has been prepared in Antalya for COP31, organized under the theme COP of the Future – COP of Implementation, built around three pillars: dialogue, consensus, and action.

pg:https://www.aljazeera.com/opinions/20.desc: The message of the vote is that the violent Israeli policies within occupied territory and the region will continue.
paras: There are two ways to read the results of the Israeli elections. One way would be to see them as a defeat for the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. From holding a solid majority in the 120-member Knesset, the Netanyahu bloc has been reduced to a minority of 53 members. Anti-Netanyahu lawmakers, by contrast, hold 67 seats.

Had Israel been a democracy, we would have seen scenes of celebration similar to the ones we saw this year in Hungary, Brazil and Serbia, where political forces with undemocratic tendencies were defeated. But Israel is not a democracy, and Netanyahu was not necessarily defeated.

The second, more relevant way of reading the results of the Israeli election would necessitate accepting the apartheid nature of Israel and seeing the electoral arithmetic through that prism. In this case, Netanyahu won because he secured 53 seats in the Knesset – five more than the anti-Netanyahu Jewish bloc.

pg:https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trum.desc: The president said in an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes” that he would like to work out a deal with Democrats on immigration.

pg:https://iol.co.za/entertainment/2026-.desc: The British comedian has been convicted of rape and three sexual assaults following a wave of #MeToo allegations
paras: British comedian and actor Russell Brand faces a lengthy prison sentence after a London jury convicted him of rape and three sexual assaults over offenses dating back more than two decades.

The 51-year-old was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday of raping a woman at his London home in 2009 and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009. The jury acquitted him of two additional rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand, who denied all seven charges, was remanded in custody, and will be sentenced on Monday. Rape carries four to 19 years in prison, with a maximum penalty of life imprisonment. Sexual assault carries a maximum sentence of ten years.
